# Item

A row with media, a title, a description and actions.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** A list such as saved applications, each with worded secondary buttons. Not records compared cell by cell.

- **Use it when:** Lists of things such as people, files or settings, each with a few actions.
- **Not when:** Records people compare cell by cell (a table).

Instead:

- [Card](./card.md): A larger unit with more content.
- [Table](./table.md): Records compared across columns.

## Why it works this way

Item looks the way it does because of 5 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Item, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-elevation-definition"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What separates groups on the page?</b><code>elevation.definition</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Lines</div><p>Strong borders separate groups at any zoom.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>default</b>: A row with no border is hard to see at high zoom; borders do the work.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>outline</b>: Each saved application, with a strong border that separates it at any zoom.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Toggle: default</code> <code>Toggle: outline</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Item decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-elevation-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How soft are shadows?</b><code>elevation.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">No shadows</div><p>No shadows; borders do the work.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>default</b>: A row with no border is hard to see at high zoom; borders do the work.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>outline</b>: Each saved application, with a strong border that separates it at any zoom.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Item decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many signals carry each meaning?</b><code>accessibility.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Three: color, icon and word</div><p>Never color alone.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>muted</b>: A fill alone marks a row by color; status goes in a badge with an icon and a word.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code> <code>Badge: neutral</code> <code>Badge: success</code> <code>Badge: warning</code> <code>Badge: danger</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Item decision would reopen</small><p>and 1 answer that follow from it: <b>Status and messages</b>.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the smallest target?</b><code>accessibility.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Large</div><p>Large targets for tremor and touch.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Every row. Large targets help people with motor needs.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>sm</b>: Large targets help people with motor needs; nothing smaller.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: default</code> <code>Button: compact</code> <code>Button: large</code> <code>Toggle: default</code> <code>Toggle: sm</code> <code>Toggle: lg</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Item decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-spacing-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many densities exist?</b><code>spacing.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One</div><p>One density; no compact mode to fail people.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Item</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>sm</b>: Large targets help people with motor needs; nothing smaller.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Item decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add item
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Item reads 30 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Item's tokens to change Item alone.
